newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops thrust out of Lebanon border zone.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops thrust out of Lebanon border zone.

text.p: Israeli troops thrust out of their self-declared border security zone in south Lebanon in an overnight attack on anti-Israeli guerrillas, the army said on Monday.
Security sources said soldiers in helicopters and planes and on foot fought the guerrillas.
An army statement said "a number of terrorists" were injured while all of the Israeli troops returned safely.
It said an army force acted north of the security zone in an area around Nabatiyeh where it encountered and fought "a terrorist group: before returning.
Iranian-backed Hizbollah guerrillas operate in the area to try to oust Israel from its 15-km (nine-mile) border zone in south Lebanon.

Israel carved out the zone in 1985 after withdrawing the bulk of its 1982 invasion force from Lebanon. Israeli troops and their militia allies in the South Lebanon Army patrol the zone with the declared aim of guarding Israel's northern border from guerrilla attack.
